citation: CPF Act 1953 s.7(6)–(7) (SSO, current as at 29 Sep 2026): s.7(6) says the employee share is recovered "from the wages in respect of which the contribution is payable at the time of payment of those wages and not otherwise". s.7(7), for wages paid at intervals of less than a month where the month's wages are "likely to exceed $500": (a) the employer "may deduct … at the time of each payment in the month the appropriate proportion of such sum as would be recoverable … if paid at the same rate throughout the month"; (b) it "must make such adjustment as may be necessary on the occasion of the last payment in that month", and if the month's wages do not exceed $500 it "must forthwith refund to the employee the amount of the deductions".
reason: SPLIT and LAST follow s.7(7) (golden). FIRST cutoff breaches s.7(7)(a): full month's employee share deducted from the first half. Finding: The engine assesses CPF over the MONTH. With `semi_monthly_statutory_cutoff` SPLIT, each half takes ½ of the month's estimate (the half's wage × 2) and the last half trues up. With LAST, the last payment prices the month whole, and a weekly company is always LAST. With FIRST, the company default, the first half takes the whole month's estimated employee share. The true-up is `month − already`, unfloored, so a month that ends at $500 or less refunds through a negative employee line at the last payment. Evidence: Golden "at a sub-monthly cadence the employee CPF share is taken in proportion or at the last payment…" in `tests/statutory-golden-sg.test.ts`, in all five sealed months: SPLIT 300/255 then 300/255; LAST 0/0 then 600/510; weekly March 2026 0/0 until the last week, then 600/510. There is no refund golden: equal halves cannot produce an estimate above $500 with an actual month at or below it, and the SG catalogue has no ordinary ad hoc to vary one half. Legacy status: Partial [IN-SYSTEM 2026-09-29] (FIRST cutoff).
